validity.recommendation: Status/CancelledYear are cited to three articles that do not discuss this pipeline at all. Either find a source that directly states the Leviathan→Idku/Damietta offshore concept was abandoned, or downgrade: keep Status=cancelled but set ShelvedCancelledType=inferred (per standing rule 2) and drop the three mismatched refs from the Status/Cancelled [ref] cells — do not present them as evidence for the cancellation.
validity.researcher_notes: The three refs on Status[ref]/Cancelled[ref] (jpt.spe.org 'Chevron greenlights construction of Israel's Nitzana gas pipeline to Egypt'; rigzone 'New pipeline paves way for increased Israeli gas exports to Egypt' 10-Jul-2026; mees.com 'Israel-Egypt onshore gas pipeline advances with cabinet approval' 12-May-2023) all pass url_verifier as live 200s, which is why the worklist's mechanical check marked them 'ok' — but I read all three in full and NONE of them mentions the Leviathan platform, an offshore/subsea pipeline to Idku or Damietta, or any cancellation of that concept. All three are about a DIFFERENT, still-advancing project: the ONSHORE Nitzana pipeline (Ramat Hovav → Nitzana border crossing, ~65 km overland, Chevron-financed, targeted completion 2028) and the already-completed EMG/Ashkelon subsea expansion. jpt.spe.org explicitly frames Nitzana as an alternative 'differs from subsea options'; mees.com describes a 65 km onshore line via Sinai with no mention of Idku/Damietta/Nitzana by name; rigzone covers the completed EMG capacity expansion plus the still-conditional future Nitzana route. None of the three states or implies that the 2021-proposed offshore Leviathan→Idku/Damietta pipeline (the actual subject of this GEM row) was formally cancelled — the mechanical verifier passed because it matched a generic token (e.g. 'Egypt'/a year), not because the article corroborates the cited fact, which is exactly the false-confirmation trap the ref rules warn about. I independently searched for direct evidence the offshore Leviathan-Idku/Damietta pipeline was cancelled and found none outside of GEM's own wiki page (which repeats the identical Background prose verbatim — circular, and rule 1 bars citing it) and general overview pieces that likewise only report the Nitzana onshore alternative moving forward. So Status=cancelled is very plausibly the right real-world call (a 2021 proposal that never restarted, superseded five years later by a different onshore route, is a textbook lapsed/shelved project) but CancelledYear=2025 looks like it was back-derived from the dateline of the (unrelated) Nitzana articles rather than from any statement about this pipeline, and no source actually says 'cancelled.' This is a mis-citation, not a fabrication of the underlying fact — flagging per standing rule 2 rather than deleting the status outright.

validity.recommendation: No action needed on existence/background; optionally tighten EndLocation to name both Idku and Damietta (or note both) since every source that describes the terminus names them jointly, not Idku alone.
validity.researcher_notes: Existence, ProposalYear/Month, Background narrative, and general route (Leviathan platform, Israel → Egyptian LNG terminals) are well corroborated by THREE independent, non-GEM sources I fetched and verified live: worldoil.com (20-Feb-2021, 'undersea natural-gas pipeline' connecting Leviathan field to Egypt's LNG plants, ministries agreed to a governmental framework), jpost.com (21-Feb-2021, Steinitz/El-Molla agreed 'to connect Israel's Leviathan gas field to facilities owned by the Egyptian Liquefied Natural Gas company via an offshore pipeline'), and offshore-technology.com (describes Israel and Egypt 'planning to construct a second subsea pipeline, which will supply LNG plants of Idku and Damietta in Egypt', distinct from the existing EMG/Ashkelon subsea line). All three are genuinely independent of each other and of GEM, and none traces to abarrelfull or gem.wiki. Caveat: sources consistently describe the destination as BOTH Idku and Damietta, never Idku alone — GEM's EndLocation names only Idku LNG terminal, which narrows the sourced claim. Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are trivially correct for a gas export line and uncontroversial, but their only current ref (an archived arabnews page) could not be reached this pass (ConnectTimeout both via curl and via fetch tool) — leaving them technically unverified rather than wrong; not flagging as a concern given how low-risk the values are, but noting for the record.

summary: P8000 existence/Feb-2021 offshore Leviathan→Idku+Damietta proposal well corroborated by 3 independent sources (confirmed, caveat: sources say Idku+Damietta jointly, GEM names Idku alone); but Status=cancelled/CancelledYear=2025 are cited to three articles that are actually about an unrelated, still-advancing project (the onshore Nitzana pipeline) and never mention this pipeline or its cancellation — flagged as a spec concern, recommend ShelvedCancelledType=inferred with the mismatched refs dropped. No UNRESOLVED fills; Fuel/PipelineType rest on an unreachable archived ref (timeout, not a deletion).
